editor_note: Entry 10 is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the little-endian default against the `big` BitArray default, the caveat "tergantung apakah primitif tersebut mengubah pengaturan ini", and the contrast that Sampler/Estimator return big-endian while Executor returns little-endian.

The six rewritten headings faithfully keep the English imperative form ("Pantau, kalibrasi, dan benchmark", "Pantau parameter", "Pantau secara holistik", "Kalibrasi"), match the body's "pemantauan, kalibrasi, dan benchmarking" and do not mislead.

The six rewritten entries (6–11) are faithful and read naturally, with nothing a learner could misread. Examples: "karakterisasi noise kuantum berbasis randomisasi", "ZNE berbasis gate-folding" with "menyaring error non-Markovian", and "Circuit berkedalaman konstan … model Fermi-Hubbard 1-D dan 2-D". "execution model" is used the same way in entries 6 and 8.

The six rewritten entries (5-10) are faithful. Orbit, Parity Twine Optimizer and Constrained Quantum Optimizer are described accurately, "unfeasible with standard, SWAP-heavy transpilation" becomes "tidak mungkin dicapai dengan metode transpilasi standar yang sarat SWAP", and "XY-mixer, bukan lewat suku penalti" keeps the contrast. Circuit function and Application function stay in English as house style requires. The one slip is register: entry 7 addresses the reader as "kamu" ("memungkinkan kamu mengaktifkan..."), but every other entry on the page uses "Anda". A native editor would change it to "Anda" so the page reads consistently.

examples.line_approx: Fungsi ini menerapkan penekanan error ... dan memungkinkan kamu mengaktifkan, menonaktifkan, atau membandingkan
examples.source: and lets you enable, disable, or compare each technique against the raw circuit
examples.translation: dan memungkinkan kamu mengaktifkan, menonaktifkan, atau membandingkan setiap teknik dengan Circuit mentahnya
examples.suggested: dan memungkinkan Anda mengaktifkan, menonaktifkan, atau membandingkan setiap teknik dengan Circuit mentahnya
examples.why: Only this entry uses "kamu"; the rest of the page (entries 13-58, 129) uses "Anda". Mixing the two forms of address on one page reads as uneven.

editor_note: Entry 5 is accurate and would not mislead a learner. The migration scenarios, "Sampler dan Estimator sisi klien", "primitif V1", "terverifikasi IBM" and the promise of more skills "dalam waktu dekat" all match the English, and the "kamu" register holds. One small slip: the bold lead-in uses the English plural "Skills baru". Indonesian does not add -s for plurals, and the rest of the page, including later in the same entry, uses the bare loanword "skill", so the lead-in should be "Skill baru untuk agen".

examples.source: **New skills for agents**
examples.translation: **Skills baru untuk agen**
examples.suggested: **Skill baru untuk agen**
examples.why: Indonesian does not mark plurals with an English -s. Entries 0, 1 and 3, and the rest of entry 5, all use "skill", so "Skills" is inconsistent and reads as English left in the text.

editor_note: Entry 129 says the same thing as the English and would not mislead a learner: the client-side capture of design intent, the costly variant generation moved to the server, and the Executor generating and running randomized variants in Qiskit Runtime all come through. Two small things remain. The link texts '[Samplomatic library]' and '[Executor primitive]' keep English word order and the English word 'primitive', while this file elsewhere says 'primitif Qiskit' (entries 45, 46, 51) and 'masing-masing primitif' (entry 61). Also, 'lapisan-lapisan tepat dalam circuit Anda tempat menerapkan Pauli-twirling' copies the English sentence structure and reads stiffly.

examples.source: The new [Executor primitive](/guides/directed-execution-model#executor-primitive) will then follow your directives
examples.translation: [Executor primitive](/guides/directed-execution-model#executor-primitive) yang baru kemudian akan mengikuti arahan Anda
examples.suggested: [Primitif Executor](/guides/directed-execution-model#executor-primitive) yang baru kemudian akan mengikuti arahan Anda
examples.why: The file uses 'primitif' everywhere else (entries 45, 46, 51, 61). The English word order and the untranslated 'primitive' here are inconsistent with that.

examples.source: you can use the [Samplomatic library] to define the exact layers in your circuits to apply Pauli-twirling and to inject noise

examples.why: 'lapisan-lapisan tepat ... tempat menerapkan' copies the English structure and reads stiffly. Indonesian puts the head noun first, so 'library Samplomatic' is more natural.

editor_note: None of the eight rewritten entries (5-12) would mislead a learner. Their meaning, caveats and qualifiers match the English, for example "di sebagian besar kasus" and "bukan isi kodenya" in entry 9, and "tanpa mengorbankan performa" in entry 12. Two small things are worth fixing. In entry 6, the open English "they" becomes "keduanya" ("the two of them"), which commits to exactly two tools when the source does not. In entry 12, "membuka logika mitigasi error" is a literal calque of "exposes"; "memperlihatkan" or "mengekspos" reads more naturally.

examples.source: Together with Samplomatic, they make up the directed execution model
examples.translation: Bersama dengan Samplomatic, keduanya membentuk directed execution model
examples.suggested: Bersama dengan Samplomatic, tools tersebut membentuk directed execution model
examples.why: 'keduanya' means 'the two of them' and adds a count the English never states. The neutral 'tools tersebut' keeps the original reference.

examples.source: exposes the error mitigation logic applied to your workloads
examples.translation: membuka logika mitigasi error yang diterapkan pada beban kerja kamu
examples.suggested: memperlihatkan logika mitigasi error yang diterapkan pada beban kerja kamu
examples.why: 'membuka' (open) is a literal rendering of 'exposes'. A native technical writer would use 'memperlihatkan' or 'mengekspos' to say that the logic is made visible.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. The table semantics are intact: the conditional reset on Heron versus the unconditional reset on Nighthawk r2, DC as the default TLS bias, and the slow_gates_ac/session tip. Terms are consistent (gate lambat, mitigasi error, estimasi observable, kalibrasi alternatif) and the register is "kamu" throughout. The one slip is in entry [21], where "some additional decoherence" became "dekoherensi tambahan". Dropping "some" makes the cost of slow cz gates sound slightly larger, so a qualifier like "sedikit" should go back in.

examples.source: which causes some additional decoherence
examples.translation: yang menyebabkan dekoherensi tambahan
examples.suggested: yang menyebabkan sedikit dekoherensi tambahan
examples.why: The English hedges the amount with 'some'. Dropping it slightly strengthens the downside claim. It does not mislead, but the qualifier should be kept.

editor_note: Entry 24 is faithful and natural: "kunjungi dokumentasi [panduan] dan [referensi API]" keeps both links, and "Silakan kirimkan masukan dan laporkan bug di repositori [GitHub]-nya" matches the English invitation and uses the informal register.

All 10 rewritten entries say what the English says and read naturally, for example "Teknik mitigasi dan supresi error", "Model eksekusi terarah" and "[Opsi `zne_mitigation`] dengan [`pea`] sebagai amplifier"; the PEA-needs-ZNE condition in entry 42 is kept, and the informal "kamu" is used throughout.

The 20 rewritten entries keep their meaning. The PEA caveat "(Harus mengaktifkan ZNE juga)" in [26] survives, and so do the v0.50.0 client-side noise-learning-job note in [49] and the label pattern "Cara mengaktifkan / Referensi API / Opsi penting". The one defect is the cross-reference link text in [7] and [41], "Pengaturan noise management kustom". It mixes word orders and leaves "noise management" in English, while the target heading [47] and the rest of the page use "manajemen noise". The link text should match the heading word for word, "Pengaturan manajemen noise kustom".

examples.source: See the [Custom noise management settings](#advanced-error) section
examples.translation: Lihat bagian [Pengaturan noise management kustom](#advanced-error)
examples.suggested: Lihat bagian [Pengaturan manajemen noise kustom](#advanced-error)
examples.why: The link text differs from the heading it points to ([47] 'Pengaturan manajemen noise kustom') and from 'manajemen noise' as used everywhere else on the page.

examples.source: as described in [Custom noise management settings](#advanced-error).
examples.translation: seperti yang dijelaskan di [Pengaturan noise management kustom](#advanced-error).
examples.suggested: seperti yang dijelaskan di [Pengaturan manajemen noise kustom](#advanced-error).
examples.why: This is the same mismatch with the section heading as in [7]. A reader looking for the section by its title will not find this wording.

editor_note: Entry 43 keeps the full meaning in natural Indonesian: "mendokumentasikan opsi dari versi terbaru `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" for the latest-version scope and "kunjungi [referensi API ...] dan pilih versi sebelumnya" for the instruction to pick an older version.

Entry 54 is faithful and reads naturally: all five recommendations are kept, 'directed execution model' is rendered as 'model eksekusi terarah' in both bullets, 'opsi Executor' and 'dokumentasi Samplomatic' match the rest of the page, and the tutorial title rightly stays in English.

The four rewritten entries (32, 34-36) match the English: the shapes (28, 10, 1024, 3) and (28, 10, 1, 3) are kept, the one-shot reason for measurement_flips.meas is kept, and 'indeks 0 menyimpan hasil bit klasik 0, yaitu bit paling tidak signifikan' gives the little-endian point correctly.

Entry 11 is faithful and keeps the restriction ("hanya bisa memproses informasi yang dienkode dalam samplex"), so nothing in it would mislead a learner. One small fix: the link text "Samplomatic guides" was left in English in the middle of an Indonesian sentence. Entry 24 on the same page translates its link text ("referensi API `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"), so this one should read "panduan Samplomatic". Using "dienkode" here and "dikodekan" in entry 6 is defensible and not flagged.

examples.source: Refer to the [Samplomatic guides](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/addons/samplomatic/index) to understand restrictions.
examples.translation: Lihat [Samplomatic guides](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/addons/samplomatic/index) untuk memahami batasannya.
examples.suggested: Lihat [panduan Samplomatic](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/addons/samplomatic/index) untuk memahami batasannya.
examples.why: The generic word 'guides' is not a product name. Entry 24 translates its link text, so this English link text in Indonesian prose is unnatural and inconsistent with the rest of the page.

editor_note: Entries 12 and 15 are faithful and would not mislead a learner. Terms are correct and used the same way throughout: 'observable berbobot rendah/tinggi', 'nilai ekspektasi tak bias', 'penekanan error', 'subruang yang layak' for feasible subspace, 'tanpa pelatihan parameter variasional'. There are two small slips in entry 15. In the HI-VQE row, 'masing-masing hingga beberapa orde besaran' adds 'hingga' ('up to'), which slightly softens 'by orders of magnitude'. In the QUICK-PDE row, 'kerangka VQA hibrida yang tangguh yang menghasilkan' stacks two 'yang' clauses, which reads as stiff translationese.

examples.source: outperforming some classical solutions on supercomputers or standard SQD in convergence speed or accuracy, respectively, by orders of magnitude
examples.translation: melampaui beberapa solusi klasik di superkomputer atau SQD standar dalam kecepatan konvergensi atau akurasi, masing-masing hingga beberapa orde besaran
examples.suggested: melampaui beberapa solusi klasik di superkomputer atau SQD standar dalam kecepatan konvergensi atau akurasi, masing-masing sebesar beberapa orde besaran
examples.why: 'hingga' (up to) is not in the source and slightly softens the claim. This is minor and does not mislead.

examples.source: Offers a robust hybrid VQA framework that delivers precise, scalable PDE solutions
examples.translation: Menawarkan kerangka VQA hibrida yang tangguh yang menghasilkan solusi PDE presisi dan skalabel
examples.suggested: Menawarkan kerangka VQA hibrida tangguh yang menghasilkan solusi PDE yang presisi dan skalabel
examples.why: Stacking 'yang tangguh yang menghasilkan' is a stiff calque. A native editor would drop the first 'yang'.

editor_note: Rewritten entries 25 and 27 are faithful and natural ("secara struktural setara dengan circuit asli", "gate single-qubit-nya digantikan oleh gate yang diparameterisasi", "parameter acak bagi template circuit"), with no drift, and keeping "measurement twirling" as a technique name is a defensible choice.

None of the 18 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The responsibilities split, the two recommended actions and the caveats for switching regions (qubit characteristics only in the affected region, regulatory or data-residency limits) all match the English. The one problem is inconsistent terminology. The rewritten entries 13, 14, 16 and 29 translate "disaster recovery" as "pemulihan bencana", but the unchanged entries 0, 1, 3 and 4 keep the English "disaster recovery", so one page uses both. Entry 14 glosses the term as "(disaster recovery, DR)", so the reader can still tell they mean the same thing, but the page should use one form throughout.

examples.source: Disaster recovery {#disaster-recovery}
examples.translation: Pemulihan bencana {#disaster-recovery}
examples.suggested: Use one rendering on the whole page: either keep "Disaster recovery" here as in entries 0/1/3/4, or switch those entries to "pemulihan bencana" as well.
examples.why: The page's earlier entries keep "disaster recovery" in English (e.g. "Memahami high availability dan disaster recovery"), so the same concept now appears under two names on one page.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The version notes (v0.50.0), the legacy server-side vs client-side contrast in [24]/[41], the "about 32 qubits" limit and the three mitigation options in [42]-[45] all match the English. "Committing QPU time" became "memakai waktu QPU" and "under the cover" became "di balik layar", both natural. The one slip is in [42]: "Local noisy simulation" is rendered "simulasi noisy lokal", which keeps the English adjective "noisy". The rest of the page says "berderau" ([15], [16], [17], [21]) or "dengan noise" ([10]), so [42] should follow that convention.

examples.source: Local noisy simulation cost grows exponentially with qubit count
examples.translation: Biaya simulasi noisy lokal tumbuh secara eksponensial terhadap jumlah qubit
examples.suggested: Biaya simulasi berderau lokal tumbuh secara eksponensial terhadap jumlah qubit
examples.why: The English adjective 'noisy' is kept here, but the rest of the file renders it as 'berderau' (entries 15, 16, 17, 21) or 'dengan noise' (entry 10). Readers can still follow it, but the term is used inconsistently.

editor_note: Entry 64 keeps the English meaning: logical equivalence, the Operator/unitary comparison, the caveat about measurement_flips corrections, and the StatevectorSampler/StatevectorEstimator alternative are all there. It has two wording problems. The opener "Untuk lebih lanjut" is a stiff calque of "To go further", and "Untuk melangkah lebih jauh" reads more naturally. In "expectation value dari `StatevectorSampler` atau `StatevectorEstimator` lokal yang dijalankan", the closing "yang dijalankan" is a clumsy rendering of "a local … run"; it should say these are values from a local run.

examples.source: To go further, you can verify that each randomization...
examples.translation: Untuk lebih lanjut, kamu bisa memverifikasi...
examples.suggested: Untuk melangkah lebih jauh, kamu bisa memverifikasi...
examples.why: 'Untuk lebih lanjut' is an incomplete calque. A native technical writer would write 'Untuk melangkah lebih jauh' or 'Lebih jauh lagi'.

examples.source: by comparing expectation values from a local `StatevectorSampler` or `StatevectorEstimator` run
examples.translation: dengan membandingkan expectation value dari `StatevectorSampler` atau `StatevectorEstimator` lokal yang dijalankan
examples.suggested: dengan membandingkan expectation value dari eksekusi lokal menggunakan `StatevectorSampler` atau `StatevectorEstimator`
examples.why: The relative clause 'lokal yang dijalankan' at the end is awkward and follows English word order. The point is that the values come from a local run, and the sentence should say that directly.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [21] keeps the soft advice "consider using" as "pertimbangkan untuk menggunakan" and renders annotated boxes as "box yang dianotasi", the same term used in [17] and [19]. [27] gives "kamu bisa memberikan opsi `twirling_strategy` ke fungsi", which matches how "diberikan ke" is used for passing things in [5] and [24].

Both rewritten entries match the English: the table in [46] renders the categories as "Gate satu-qubit / Gate dua-qubit / Gate fraksional / Instruksi non-unitary" with every link intact, and [65] correctly says Target is "objek yang berisi semua informasi yang diperlukan untuk mentranspilasi circuit" and "mencakup error dan durasi instruksi".

Entry 18 is faithful and reads naturally: the client-side/server-side split ("alat sisi klien" for uploading and running remote programs, "alat sisi server" for "mendistribusikan komputasi dan mengelola data") is kept, the `python` 3.11+ requirement is unchanged, and Qiskit Serverless stays in English.

Entry 26 is faithful and natural. It keeps every listed resource: 'kode etik', 'perjanjian lisensi PDF untuk kontributor individu dan korporat', 'strategi versi', and 'panduan kontributor dan maintainer'.

The six rewritten entries keep the meaning of the English; none of them would mislead a learner. Entries 5 and 6 switch to the informal "kamu" ("browser kamu", "pertamamu"), while entries 13, 14 and 17 and the rest of the page use "Anda". Within the delta, "circuit" appears three ways: "Circuit" (entry 6), "Sirkuit" (entry 14 title) and "circuit" (entry 14, Construct circuits card), and entry 49 also has "sirkuit". The card text "jalankan tiga cara" in entry 14 is missing a preposition and should read "jalankan dengan tiga cara".

examples.source: Run your first quantum circuit
examples.translation: Jalankan Circuit kuantum pertamamu
examples.suggested: Jalankan sirkuit kuantum pertama Anda
examples.why: Uses the kamu-form '-mu' and a capitalized 'Circuit', while the matching card title in entry 14 reads 'Sirkuit Kuantum Pertama Anda'.

examples.source: run the code right here in your browser
examples.translation: jalankan kodenya langsung di browser kamu
examples.suggested: jalankan kodenya langsung di browser Anda
examples.why: 'kamu' here, while entries 13, 14 and 17 and the rest of the page use 'Anda'.

examples.source: Construct circuits / building quantum circuits
examples.translation: Membangun circuit / membangun circuit kuantum
examples.suggested: Membangun sirkuit / membangun sirkuit kuantum
examples.why: The same entry already uses 'Sirkuit' in the Hello World title, so the page shows Circuit, Sirkuit, circuit and sirkuit for one concept.

examples.source: run it three ways
examples.translation: jalankan tiga cara
examples.suggested: jalankan dengan tiga cara
examples.why: Missing the preposition, which reads as clipped machine translation.

editor_note: The rewrite of entry 42 says the same thing as the English and would not mislead a learner. It keeps every point: fermionic creation and annihilation operators, the (tak-terbedakan) caveat, the requirement for a bosonic operator on IBM Quantum QPUs, Pauli operators as "Hermitian sekaligus uniter", and Jordan Wigner as one of the simplest of several mappings. One phrase is a calque: "antisimetri di bawah pertukaran" copies the English "under exchange" word for word. Indonesian physics writing uses "antisimetri terhadap pertukaran". Terminology matches the rest of the page (fermionik, bosonik, operator kreasi/anihilasi, pemetaan).

examples.source: correspondingly subject to antisymmetry under exchange
examples.translation: dan karenanya tunduk pada antisimetri di bawah pertukaran
examples.suggested: dan karenanya bersifat antisimetris terhadap pertukaran
examples.why: "di bawah" copies the English "under" word for word. Indonesian physics texts express symmetry with respect to an operation with "terhadap". The meaning is unchanged, so this does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. I checked the negations and caveats in the hard places: the even-parity limits, the d=2 blind spots, the warnings that gamma is not a hardware guarantee, and the caveat that error detection is not unbiased. None of them is inverted or dropped. The problem is that core terms switch between English and Indonesian from section to section, sometimes inside one paragraph: 'error' and 'kesalahan' are mixed (for example in [139] and [145]); 'check' is 'pemeriksaan' through Part 1 and 'check' from [145] on; 'syndrome' becomes 'sindrom' in [129]–[145] and [306]; 'detection region' and 'daerah deteksi' alternate; 'lapisan' and 'layer' alternate; 'fidelity' is 'fidelitas' once in [160]; 'post-selection rate' and 'tingkat post-selection' alternate; and the heading is 'Uji pemahamanmu' in places and 'Cek pemahamanmu' in others. [145] also renders 'a fixed syndrome-extraction block' as 'blok ekstraksi sindrom tetap', which readers can take as 'is still applied' rather than 'fixed-size'.

examples.source: whether the underlying fault was a gate error in the payload, a gate error in the syndrome extraction, or a measurement readout error
examples.translation: apakah kesalahan dasarnya berupa error gate pada payload, error gate pada ekstraksi sindrom, atau error pembacaan pengukuran
examples.suggested: apakah fault yang mendasarinya berupa error gate pada payload, error gate pada ekstraksi syndrome, atau error readout pengukuran
examples.why: 'kesalahan' and 'error' are mixed inside one sentence, and 'sindrom' here clashes with 'syndrome' in the rest of the file.

examples.source: and a fixed syndrome-extraction block is applied to every shot
examples.translation: dan blok ekstraksi sindrom tetap diterapkan di setiap shot
examples.suggested: dan blok ekstraksi syndrome berukuran tetap diterapkan di setiap shot
examples.why: 'tetap' after the noun can be read as 'still applied' rather than 'fixed-size', which blurs the point that the overhead is a fixed block.

examples.source: that constraint can be used as the check
examples.translation: batasan itu bisa dipakai sebagai pemeriksaan
examples.suggested: batasan itu bisa dipakai sebagai check
examples.why: 'check' is 'pemeriksaan' through Part 1 but 'check' from [145] on, so one core concept appears under two names.

examples.source: The fidelity gain from each extra check
examples.translation: Peningkatan fidelitas dari tiap check ekstra
examples.suggested: Peningkatan fidelity dari tiap check ekstra
examples.why: 'fidelity' is kept in English everywhere else (Hellinger fidelity, fidelity pasca-seleksi); 'fidelitas' appears only here.

examples.source: Coherent Pauli checks (Sections 2.2-2.3) provided the algebraic foundation
examples.translation: Check Pauli koheren (Bagian 2.2-2.3) menyediakan fondasi aljabar
examples.suggested: Coherent Pauli checks (Bagian 2.2-2.3) menyediakan fondasi aljabar
examples.why: The method is named 'coherent Pauli check(s)' everywhere else, including the [163] heading; the wrap-up should use the same name.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The M3, TREX, ZNE and PEC explanations, the readout-error table and the 6- vs 30-qubit PEC conclusions match the English, and I found no drift that would mislead a learner. The page reads as if different translators did different sections: the first third uses "derau", "keadaan" and "kanal", while later sections switch to "noise", "state" and "channel", and "observable" also appears as "observabel" from [422]. The register also switches between "Anda" ([61], [262], [289]) and "kamu" ([118], [136], [412]). There are a few calques too: "PEC memperkenalkan tidak ada bias sistematis" ([227]), "qubit ke-$i^\text{th}$" ([136]), and "yang sebelumnya membutuhkan" for "would otherwise have required" ([415]).

examples.source: PEC therefore introduces **no systematic bias** in expectation
examples.translation: Jadi PEC memperkenalkan **tidak ada bias sistematis** secara ekspektasi
examples.suggested: Jadi PEC **tidak memperkenalkan bias sistematis** secara ekspektasi
examples.why: This copies the English 'introduces no' word order. Indonesian puts the negation on the verb.

examples.source: noise channels that would otherwise have required non-physical steps
examples.translation: kanal noise yang sebelumnya membutuhkan langkah non-fisik
examples.suggested: kanal noise yang tanpa cara ini akan membutuhkan langkah non-fisik
examples.why: 'sebelumnya' means 'previously', so the sentence now says these channels used to require such steps. The English says they would need them without this method.

examples.source: We choose an observable to estimate.
examples.translation: Kita memilih observabel untuk diestimasi.
examples.suggested: Kita memilih observable untuk diestimasi.
examples.why: Most of the file uses 'observable', but from [422] it becomes 'observabel'. The same split happens with derau/noise, keadaan/state and kanal/channel.

examples.source: if you apply measurement twirling during the calibration used in M3
examples.translation: kalau kamu menerapkan measurement twirling saat kalibrasi yang dipakai di M3
examples.suggested: kalau Anda menerapkan measurement twirling saat kalibrasi yang dipakai di M3
examples.why: The file switches between 'Anda' ([61], [262], [289]) and 'kamu' ([118], [136], [412]). It should use one form of address throughout.

examples.source: for the $i^\text{th}$ qubit
examples.translation: untuk qubit ke-$i^\text{th}$
examples.suggested: untuk qubit ke-$i$
examples.why: 'ke-' and the English 'th' both mark the ordinal, so it is marked twice. Use 'ke-$i$'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English in meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problem is the term for "error suppression". Entries 6 and 7 use "supresi error", but the title, the H2 heading and the intro paragraph [1], [4] and [5] all use "penekanan error". Within one page a reader could take these for two different concepts, so entries 6 and 7 should use "penekanan error". Also, "animasi berharga" is a calque of "valuable animations"; "animasi yang berguna" reads more naturally.

examples.source: This video gives an overview of error suppression ... explores some types of error suppression using Qiskit.
examples.translation: Video ini memberikan gambaran umum tentang supresi error ... beberapa jenis supresi error memakai Qiskit.
examples.suggested: Video ini memberikan gambaran umum tentang penekanan error ... beberapa jenis penekanan error menggunakan Qiskit.
examples.why: The rest of the page ([1], [4], [5]) says 'penekanan error'. Using 'supresi error' only here makes the page inconsistent.

examples.source: an overview of quantum error suppression techniques
examples.translation: gambaran umum tentang teknik supresi error kuantum
examples.suggested: gambaran umum tentang teknik penekanan error kuantum
examples.why: Same inconsistency as entry 6: the page's established term is 'penekanan error'.

examples.source: including some valuable animations for picturing how they work
examples.translation: termasuk beberapa animasi berharga untuk membayangkan cara kerjanya

editor_note: The four rewritten titles keep the English meaning and nothing in them would mislead a learner ("Kimia kuantum dengan VQE", "Gunakan komputer kuantum hari ini", "Qiskit di kelas - ilmu komputer", "Qiskit di kelas - mekanika kuantum"). The problem is capitalization. These four use sentence case, but every other course title in this list uses Indonesian Title Case, for example "Dasar-Dasar Informasi Kuantum", "Komputasi Kuantum dalam Praktik" and "Desain Algoritma Variasional". On a page that is a list of titles the mix stands out, so the four should use Title Case like the rest.

The meaning holds throughout, including the variational-bound, noise-tolerance and M_J-at-product-stage arguments. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Terms and register drift in the last 40%, though: "eksekusi" becomes "run", "Langkah 2" becomes "Step 2", "teori perturbasi" becomes "teori gangguan", "nilai eigen" becomes "eigenvalue", "perangkat keras" becomes "hardware", and "Anda" switches to "kamu" in [140]/[145]. Two local slips: [105] says "setiap orbital sd berlangsung ℓ genap", using the wrong verb ("takes place"), and [164] renders "core energy" as "energi inti" when the file uses "core" elsewhere, which risks reading as "nuclear energy". "batas atas yang ketat" ([106], [119]) for "rigorous upper bound" can be read as "tight bound", while later entries keep "rigorous". It would be better to use one term.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the long caveat in [58] about filtering diagonal terms and the advice on pruning versus recovery in [91] and [93]. Nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few things. The workflow headings are inconsistent: "Step 1"/"Step 2" are left in English, but [78]/[80] use "Langkah 3"/"Langkah 4". "Modest subspace" in [87] becomes "subruang sederhana", which reads as "simple" rather than "moderately sized". The ordinal in [20] is doubled ("ke-$k_{th}$"). The verb for sampling switches between "men-sampel", "disampel" and "di-sampling".

editor_note: Entry 18 is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the safety caveat intact ("Sebelum kamu melakukannya, sel ini tidak menyimpan apa pun ... tidak akan pernah menimpa akun yang sudah kamu simpan sebelumnya"), the step-4/step-5 references are correct, and the register is the informal "kamu".

Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 38 ("Simulasikan evolusi waktu model Ising medan transversal") is faithful and natural. Entry 37 leaves "state" in English ("state Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger"), but the rest of the page translates it as "keadaan": "keadaan kuantum" in [28], "keadaan dasar" in [18] and "keadaan-dasar" in [33]. That is a within-file term inconsistency, and "keadaan GHZ" would match the page's own convention.

editor_note: I checked all 60 rewritten entries against the English and none of them would mislead a learner. The numbers, negations and caveats all carry over: the -40.472331 MeV lower bound, the rule that `--mode pooled` is rejected with `--bitstrings-dir`, the 11 jobs × 4,096 shots, and the point that an excitation energy cannot detect a constant offset. The problems are within-file consistency. 'Pooled' appears as 'terpool' (entry 5) and as 'gabungan' (entries 1 and 181). The Fortran block mixes 'determinant Slater', 'subspace' and 'variational' (entry 181) with 'determinan', 'subruang' and 'variasional' elsewhere. 'Two-body' appears as 'dua-body', 'two-body' and 'dua-benda', and 'shell sd' as 'shell $sd$' and 'kulit $sd$'. Entry 168 also slips into formal 'Anda' where the rest of the page uses 'kamu'.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries misleads. Entries 18 and 65 are faithful and natural ("penekanan dan mitigasi error", "pass transpilasi", "box beranotasi"), and Qiskit Runtime stays in English as required. Entry 71 keeps the meaning but reads like a calque in two places. "berhati-hati khusus untuk melacak" is not idiomatic Indonesian; "ekstra hati-hati dalam melacak" is what a native writer would use. The causal clause "sebagai akibat dari bagaimana urutan qubit ditangkap" copies the English "as a result of how" word for word; "karena cara urutan qubit dicatat" reads more naturally.

examples.suggested: Perlu dicatat bahwa kita harus ekstra hati-hati dalam melacak urutan qubit.
examples.why: 'berhati-hati khusus' is an unidiomatic literal rendering of 'take special care'.

editor_note: Entry 126 is faithful and natural: "memetakan suku Pauli ini ke bentuk kanonik yang diharapkan oleh `Executor`" and "urutan qubit kanonik" keep the meaning exactly, and "suku Pauli" matches its use in entries 125 and 135.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveats that matter were kept: the claim of no quantum advantage in [21] and [55], the brute-force caveat in [43], and "nothing else about the method does" in [46]. The issues are calques. "Couple(s)" is rendered as the non-standard verb "mengopel" in [35] and [48], which also reads like "mengepel" (to mop). "Sweep" is rendered literally as "menyapu/disapu/sapuan" in [9], [19] and [40], where "variasikan/menelusuri" would read more naturally. "Importance-aware" in [48] is calqued as "sadar-kepentingan". A smaller point: "objective" switches between "tujuan" and "objektif" in the file, but this does not stop the reader from following the concept.

editor_note: No passage reverses or invents a claim, but a few slips need fixing. In [72] "decays as 1/√T" became "menurun sebesar 1/√T", which reads as "decreases by 1/√T" rather than describing a scaling. [42] uses the same "sebesar 1/T" for "reduces the variance as 1/T". In [88], "sesuai dengan pemeriksa yang mendeteksi error sungguhan" is a stiff calque that hides the inference "consistent with the checks detecting real errors". The renderings also shift: "satu qubit" ([7], [15]) becomes "single-qubit" from [67] on, and the Indonesian word order "shadow tomography Pauli lokal" ([7], [43]) flips to the English order "local Pauli shadow tomography" in [75].

examples.suggested: Error pada korelator dua-qubit menurun sebanding dengan $1/\sqrt{T}$
examples.why: 'sebesar' means 'by the amount of', so a scaling law turns into a fixed decrement; 'sebanding dengan' keeps the meaning 'scales as'.

editor_note: The rewritten entries keep the meaning throughout. Counts and conditions all match the English: 1137 of 10000 shots, 49 of 120 determinants, the 0.1373 Ha gap, mean rather than sum for the weights, the order of normalization, and postselection versus recovery. Nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are consistency and wording. The page switches register partway: the Python tab addresses the reader as "Anda", and the rewritten C++ tab (entries 113-171) switches to "kamu". The rewritten entries use "hardware" (40, 107, 138, 139), while the rest of the page uses "perangkat keras". "Configuration recovery" is left as "recovery" in entry 99 but rendered as "pemulihan konfigurasi" in entries 164 and 167. There are also a few calques: "di tempat" for "in place" in entry 128, "condong" for "skews" in entry 129, and "terlalu lama" for "too old" in entry 108, which reads as "takes too long".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the late trade-off passages. In [63] and [67], δt=0.25 agrees best and the extra noise at 0.125 outweighs the smaller Trotter error, exactly as in the English. The problem is that several core terms are written in more than one way within this file. 'Expectation value' is left in English in [6] and [13] but becomes 'nilai ekspektasi' in [40] and [56]. 'State' is 'state Néel' in [18] but 'keadaan Néel' everywhere else. 'Error' appears once as 'galat' in [7] and as 'error' in every later entry. 'Workflow' in [13] and [31] alternates with 'alur kerja' in [38] and [60]. None of this misleads a learner, but a native editor would pick one form for each term.

examples.why: [40] and [56] use 'nilai ekspektasi'. Using one form for the term throughout the file would be cleaner.
